title: Ending generalisations while keeping support

captions.energy: Ending an exhausted way of speaking
captions.emotions: Feeling steadiness in a clear answer

meaning: By thoughtfully leaving exhausted generalisations behind, you can find a more dependable way to answer a specific request.
text: Some familiar words make a disagreement larger than the request itself. The Hermit in the physical position of your Vishuddha helps you explain this distinction after reflection. Death in energy supports willingness to end an exhausted way of speaking so it no longer determines every new conversation. The Emperor in emotions brings steadiness when an answer acquires understandable boundaries. Leaving an old formula behind can feel like gaining support rather than losing the conversation’s seriousness.

For example, you discuss “You never listen”, said after a particular interruption. You find words for the distinction: the account could not be finished this time, but that does not describe all your conversations. **A specific request is stronger than an endless generalisation**. You suggest leaving “never” behind when it replaces naming the action needed, and answer the actual request to finish speaking. Reliability comes from an understandable response to the present conversation, rather than a promise to repair the whole past at once.

However, wanting to secure this clarity can turn the new agreement into a rigid ban on any imprecise word. A considered explanation then starts sounding like control of speech. Death’s constructive meaning helps end the exhausted pattern of disagreement rather than a living expression of frustration. You can keep the request specific while acknowledging the strong feeling behind the exaggeration. Support does not require flawless phrases.
